description_complementaire: Aggregate min on total onwind MW at node BE, incl. existing capacity (solving.agg_p_nom_limits.include_existing = true).
note_complementaire: 2030 Belgian onshore wind floor (5000 MW) DROPPED for the realistic-potential scenarios. add_CCL_constraints groups by (location, carrier) and BE is a parent row over BEVLG + BEWAL + BEBRU, so capping Wallonia while holding the national floor does not lower the Belgian 2030 target -- it transfers the whole Walloon shortfall to Flanders. Held, the 16 500 MW PV floor would have required Flanders + Brussels to reach about 13 000 MW against roughly 7 100 today, +84 % in five years, which is not a realistic deployment assumption and is not what this sensitivity is testing. The point of the scenario is that the 2030 targets are NOT reached; a national floor that survives the regional cap contradicts that premise. Dropping rather than lowering it also avoids inventing a Flemish trajectory that neither ICEDD nor Elia published. The 2025 base-year pin (min = max) is untouched, so the calibration year still holds, and BEVLG's own rows are byte-identical to the central scenario. 2040/2050 carry no BE floor either way.
